source.title: On the Multilingual Capabilities of Very Large-Scale English Language Models
source.authors: Jordi Armengol-Estapé; Ona De Gibert Bonet; Maite Melero

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some table formatting is flattened, but the reported QA scores can be assigned to the models from the accompanying text.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates downstream performance scaling in a new setting: zero-shot Catalan tasks using GPT-3 model sizes. It reports a QA score trend by model size, but does not test pretraining-loss power laws.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling-law work but does not report results on held-out pretraining loss, extrapolation of loss, or compute-optimal training allocations. The human fluency evaluation uses only Davinci, so it does not test a scaling trend. Fine-tuned mBERT and XLM-R are reference results, not GPT-3 size-sweep results.
record.test_reason: Zero-shot Catalan XQuAD-ca QA was evaluated across four GPT-3 API sizes (Ada, Babbage, Curie, Davinci) with the same pretraining data. This is a downstream scale trend in a new setting (low-resource cross-lingual transfer), so it bears on V6. No pretraining loss, fits, compute allocation or architecture results are reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that GPT-3 shows remarkable zero-shot Catalan NLU and NLG despite Catalan being tiny in the corpus, and that zero-shot cross-lingual QA scales steeply with model size at fixed pretraining data. They note that small versions aren't usable, that tokenization is inefficient for Catalan, and that the study is limited to one language, two tasks and zero-shot. They suggest extending scaling-law studies (Kaplan et al.) to cross-lingual transfer.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares downstream zero-shot QA scores across GPT-3 API sizes in Catalan; it does not measure pretraining loss against parameters, tokens, or compute, fit power laws, or optimize compute allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The QA scaling result is for zero-shot Catalan XQuAD-ca; model size varies while pretraining data is held constant. Exact API model sizes are not clarified by OpenAI and are only suggested in the paper.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation
record.problems: The size sweep has four API models, whose exact parameter counts were not clarified. The paper reports no uncertainty for the QA scaling scores. The evidence is limited to zero-shot Catalan QA and does not measure pretraining loss.
record.rows_left_out: The XLM-RoBERTa and mBERT fine-tuned reference scores in Table 2 were omitted because they are not GPT-3 size-sweep results. The human sentence-rating results in Table 3 were omitted because only Davinci was evaluated.

untested.parts: Whether the trend is quantitatively predictable: no curve is fitted or extrapolated, and there is no relation to pretraining loss. Only one task (zero-shot extractive QA in Catalan) has a size sweep; generation was evaluated on Davinci only.
Not tested: no pretraining loss is reported.
Not tested: there is no loss-based power-law fit for cross-lingual transfer. The authors only suggest this as future work.

record.verdict_notes: Model sizes are third-party estimates. There is no uncertainty or repeated sampling (temperature 0.7). The human evaluation reports 3.89 in the text but 3.83 in Table 3; this is irrelevant to scaling. The record's omission of the fine-tuned reference rows and the Davinci-only human ratings is appropriate.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether loss laws fitted on smaller runs predict much larger runs.
Effects of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
The study tests downstream scaling only for zero-shot Catalan extractive QA; it does not test other downstream tasks or performance as a function of pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations on setup and fitting choices.

relationships.condition: GPT-3 API engines (approx. 350M to 175B), zero-shot Catalan XQuAD-ca, default sampling
relationships.reason: F1 (5.26, 10.08, 16.66, 38.43) and EM (0.38, 1.13, 5.00, 17.74) rise monotonically with size (r1–r8). Only four points are reported, with inferred sizes and no fit, so this shows monotonic improvement rather than tested predictability.
relationships.display_finding: F1 increased 5.26→10.08→16.66→38.43 and exact match increased 0.38→1.13→5.00→17.74, although inferred sizes and four measurements without a fitted curve leave predictability untested.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
